submission.natural_language_explanation: L2/H1 is a pure previous-token head: 0.91 of its attention is on t-1 on random repeated sequences (duplicate 0.00, induction 0.00) and 0.68-0.97 at word positions of ordinary text (a sentence-final '.' gets 0.01), so its strength |W_O(z - mean z)| at a position measures how far the token BEFORE the peak stands from the head's average write, not the token it sits on: in 'The map shows Yuri in the corner.' ' Y' scores 0.00 and the next piece 'uri' 1.10, while the whole-word version 'the man' scores 0.02, and after the same piece ' methyl' the following token barely matters ('gly' 1.95, ' group' 2.22, ' here' 2.14, ' in' 2.25). Predict active (1.0-3.7, well above the 0.94 line = 0.25 x the scan's 3.747 max) when the token before the peak is a piece rather than a whole word - any non-Latin byte piece (26 of 28 tested sentences across Greek, Cyrillic, Devanagari, Bengali, Thai, Arabic/Urdu, Hebrew, Hangul, Han, German, Finnish, Turkish, Vietnamese and Afrikaans scored 1.0-2.2), a word-internal piece of a split Latin-script word or name ('ph' 1.6-3.0, 'oo' 2.06, 'ak' 1.85, 'ost' 1.85, 'ip' 1.78, 'Br' 1.72, 'Sh' 1.98, ' methyl' 1.95-2.25), or a piece of an all-caps or hex identifier ('IN' 1.45, 'JA' 1.71, hex 'bf' 2.19) - predict inactive (0.00-0.6) when every token before a candidate peak is a whole high-frequency English word, punctuation or a newline (' the', ' of', ' and', ' house', ' people', ' city', ' water' 0.00-0.19; ten all-common-word sentences 0.00-0.18; comma-separated lists of single common words 0.00-0.58; '100 200 300 400 500 600 700' 0.00), and predict only weak, at or just over the line (0.4-1.3), after an ordinary whole English content word, which crosses in about one plain sentence in six (' short and' 1.29, ' light and' 0.99, ' first item' 1.00, 'Best wishes' 1.08, ' May and' 0.93) and stays below in the rest (' warm and' 0.15, ' old man' 0.65, ' sat down' 0.64, ' run in' 0.53, ' long decline' 0.37).

rival_explanations: The head is a rare-token detector at the position it sits on, not a previous-token copier: the unusual piece should itself be strong, so ' Y' in 'Yuri', ' methyl' in 'methylglyoxal' and ' N' in 'NINJA_URL' should score as high as the pieces that follow them.

The trigger is the proper-noun word class the confound profile flags (PROPN tokens are 39% active, twice the 20% base rate): the head should fire after any capitalised name or place name, so ' John', ' Mary', ' Peter' and ' London' should be as strong as the Shostakovich fragments.

The trigger is tokenizer fragmentation alone, not rarity or script: every word the tokenizer splits into three or more pieces should fire at its later pieces, so 'antidisestablishmentarianism' (' ant','idis','establ','ishment','arian','ism') should be as strong as 'methylglyoxal', and no single-piece word should ever fire.
